newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya sells $163.4 million in T-bills.
newsitem.headline: Kenya sells $163.4 million in T-bills.

text.p: The Central Bank of Kenya sold 8.826 billion shillings ($163.4 million) in treasury bills at the weekly auction on Thursday, bank officials said.
Out of these, the bank sold 8.676 billion shillings in the main 91-day category at an average yield of 19.422 percent compared to 7.829 billion shillings at an average of 19.677 percent last week.
"We're actually hoping to bring down the rates to 18 percent by the end of June," a bank official said.

He said the systematic downward adjustment of the average yield offered on the benchmark 91-day bills was in response to complaints by commercial banks that they could not lower their lending rates because rates on t-bills were so high.
Commercial banks' lending rates average 28 percent.
In the 28-day category of T-bills, the bank sold 150 million shillings at an average yield of 16.499 percent from to eight million shillings at 16.500 percent.
The 28-day bill will suspended from next week but the 182-day bill, suspended earlier this year, will be reinstated, the bank said.
The bank invited tenders for six billion shillings of treasury bills for the next week's auction on Thursday.
